summary: Tightened the prose, corrected five overstated or wrongly tensed claims (teaching, concluded EU projects, the Meta paper's scope, the EU citation, and RC51 membership), restored CooRnet's co-developers and the paper's own quantified findings, and flagged the omitted JRC and EACEA expert roles.

flags.claim: he teaches courses on Generative AI and Media as well as Digital Social Network Analysis
flags.issue: The authoritative biography says his teaching 'has included' these courses, a dated status stamped as of August 2026; the present-tense 'teaches courses' asserts a currency the source does not. Revised to 'his teaching has included'.

flags.claim: His recent European research appointments include leading Work Package 4 on the vera.ai project and serving as a partner on the PROMPT initiative
flags.issue: Both projects are concluded per the authoritative biography (vera.ai in October 2025, PROMPT in February 2026); the original framing reads as ongoing appointments. Revised to past tense with end dates.

flags.claim: an empirical audit evaluating Meta's political content reduction policies and their influence on electoral visibility
flags.issue: OWN RESEARCH FINDINGS describe an audit of the policy's effect on Italian parliamentarians' Facebook visibility, quantified (e.g. -72% per-post reach at trough for re-elected MPs); 'electoral visibility' is a vaguer, broader framing not stated in the paper. Revised to the paper's own scope and quantification.

flags.claim: was formally cited in parliamentary proceedings at the European level
flags.issue: The authoritative biography states the paper was cited in a written question to the European Commission (E-10-2026-000086); 'parliamentary proceedings' suggests something broader. Revised to the precise fact.

flags.claim: an active member of the International Communication Association, the Association of Internet Researchers, the Italian Association for Political Communication, and Research Committee 51 of the International Sociological Association
flags.issue: The authoritative biography lists current membership (as of August 2026) only in ICA, AoIR, and the Italian Association for Political Communication; for RC51 it states he 'has served on the board' — a completed role, not a current membership. Revised accordingly.
The biography omitted the co-developers Nicola Righetti and Luca Rossi named in the authoritative biography. Restored in the revision.

The authoritative biography records his service as a member of the Joint Research Centre expert group on systemic risks of very large online platforms (contributing to ECAT under DSA Article 40(12)) and his appointment as evaluator and rapporteur for EACEA (running to September 2026 as of August 2026); the biography drops both. If added, the EACEA mention must not name the specific call, topic or programme, nor print contract numbers.

flags.claim: guiding students in the computational mapping and critical analysis of complex communication ecosystems, algorithmic visibility, and emerging media technologies
flags.issue: Empty abstraction unsupported by any source and adding no information; cut in the revision.
